task: Display the switch’s compact table of port state, VLAN, duplex and speed.

teaching.hint: Start with the switch-wide port overview.
teaching.takeaway: Compare the two ends of the affected connection. A connected state can coexist with a duplex mismatch; the speed and duplex columns supply different evidence.

task: The compact table shows Fa0/24 connected, but traffic is unreliable. Display that port’s detailed state and error counters.

teaching.hint: Narrow the interface display to the named physical port.
teaching.takeaway: Compare current counters with a baseline and inspect the far end. A growing CRC count warrants investigation; it does not uniquely identify a cable fault.

task: SW1 Fa0/24 is a 2960 copper FastEthernet port. Its speed was forced during a test; both ends should use automatic speed selection. Restore SW1’s selected port.

teaching.hint: Remove the forced speed choice; duplex is a separate setting.
teaching.takeaway: Automatic speed selection must be checked at both ends. This command does not also remove a forced duplex setting.

task: SW1 Fa0/24 is a 2960 copper FastEthernet port. Its peer uses automatic negotiation. Restore automatic duplex on the selected SW1 port.

teaching.takeaway: Compare both operational displays after the change. On 10/100 Ethernet, one forced-full end and one automatic end can disagree on duplex even while the link is up.

task: SW1 Fa0/24 reports administratively down. The approved plan requires this selected port to be enabled. Correct its administrative setting.

teaching.hint: The output identifies a local configuration state.
teaching.takeaway: Removing shutdown enables the port administratively. A disconnected cable or disabled peer can still leave its operational state down, so inspect and retest afterward.
